mdx.body:
The UniversalFilter is designed to be dropped beside any table or catalog toolbar. Applying it consistently keeps filtering behaviour predictable as users move between Meshery, Kanvas, and Layer5 Cloud.

Do
  • Place the filter in the toolbar of the view it filters, next to the search field and to the right of the data set title.
  • Keep selectedFilters in the parent so the applied values can drive the query that fetches rows.
  • Use All as the reset value for an attribute — the component treats it as "not filtered" and excludes it from the badge count.
  • Perform the data fetch inside handleApplyFilter, which receives the freshly applied values as its argument.
  • Give every instance a unique id, and a data-testid when the view carries more than one filter.
  • Combine the filter with a separate search input for free-text queries, and reset pagination to the first page whenever filters are applied.

Don't
  • Use it for a single attribute — a lone select or chip group is lighter and clearer.
  • Re-fetch on every dropdown change; the component intentionally batches changes behind Apply.
  • Load unbounded option lists into a filter group. Beyond roughly a dozen options, use a searchable field instead.
  • Read selectedFilters as a free-form value — it is a flat map of attribute key to a single selected value.
  • Enable datePicker without also supplying selectedDateRange and setSelectedDateRange; the date section is skipped unless all three are present.

Filter Schemas

The filters prop is a record keyed by attribute. Each entry supplies the label shown above the select and the options offered inside it. The key is what appears in selectedFilters, so name it after the query parameter it maps to.

Field Type Description
name string Human-readable label rendered above the select, for example "Visibility".
options { label: string; value: string }[] Choices for the attribute. value is what lands in selectedFilters; label is what the user reads.
  • Declare schema objects outside the component, or memoise them — a new object identity on every render re-creates the panel contents.
  • Order keys by how often they are used; the panel renders them top to bottom in declaration order.
  • Keep value aligned with the API contract so applied filters can be forwarded to the backend without translation.
  • If a stored value is no longer present in options, the select falls back to the first available option rather than rendering blank.

Date Range Filtering

Set datePicker and supply a controlled selectedDateRange of the shape { startDate: Date; endDate: Date } together with its setter. The section renders a quick-range select and a pair of date-time pickers.

  • The range is applied immediately when it changes — unlike the attribute selects, it does not wait for Apply. Keep the handler cheap, or debounce the fetch it triggers.
  • The pickers keep the range coherent: moving the start past the end pushes the end forward, and moving the end before the start pulls the start back.
  • Seed selectedDateRange with a sensible default window rather than leaving it empty, so the view always has a bounded query.
  • The date pickers rely on the optional peer dependencies @mui/x-date-pickers and date-fns. Install both in any project that enables datePicker.

Quick Date Options

Quick ranges are presets that fill both pickers in one action. When quickDateRanges is omitted, the component ships with Last 7 days, Last 30 days, Last 3 months, Last 6 months, and Last 1 year.

  • Each option is { label: string; getRange: () => { startDate: Date; endDate: Date } }. Compute dates inside getRange so "last 7 days" stays relative to now.
  • Override the defaults only when the domain calls for it — an audit log may want Last 24 hours, a billing view This month.
  • Keep labels short and unambiguous; they are read in a narrow select and repeated on mobile in the bottom sheet.
  • The quick-range select does not stay visually selected after use. It is an action that seeds the pickers, and the resulting window is shown by the start and end fields.

Active Filters
  • The badge counts entries in selectedFilters whose value is set and is not All, giving users a glance-able sense of how narrow the current view is.
  • To clear everything, reset selectedFilters to All for each key and call the same handler the filter uses, so the data set and the badge stay in step.
  • Set showAllOption to false only when an attribute must always be constrained; the badge will then include that attribute permanently.
  • For views where the applied filters need to stay visible after the panel closes, render chips from selectedFilters beside the trigger — the state already lives in the parent.
  • Reflect applied filters in the URL when the view is shareable, so a filtered table survives a reload.
